clue.text: Queen to disappear going round overcome

indicators.note: one piece going round another means it surrounds it, so the second sits inside the first

parts.note: to disappear is to vanish

explanation.surface: A monarch makes herself scarce, circling around to defeat someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' is the container signal; 'Queen' here is the abbreviation Qu., not the usual ER or R.
explanation.definitionFit: To overcome an enemy is to conquer or defeat them utterly.

clue.text: Starry semicircular moulding Georgia left

indicators.note: left in the sense of departed: the state's abbreviation walks out of the moulding word

parts.note: an astragal is a small convex moulding, semicircular in section, round a column
GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: A star-studded architectural feature has been left behind by someone from Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' removes GA from ASTRAGAL, an architectural term many solvers will need to look up.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to the stars, so starry is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Audibly refer to a portion

indicators.note: audibly tells us the words are to be heard spoken, not read as spelt

parts.note: to refer to something by citing it is to quote; spoken with the following 'a' it runs together

explanation.surface: An instruction to mention aloud one share of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Audibly' signals that QUOTE A, said aloud, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An allotted share or fixed allocation is a portion of the whole.

clue.text: Part of Cambridgeshire, sounds like part of cathedral

indicators.note: sounds like says that the spoken words match a different spelling

parts.note: an aisle is a passage running alongside the nave; the cathedral meant is Ely's, so this is the aisle belonging to Ely

explanation.surface: A tour-guide remark that a district of Cambridgeshire shares its name with a bit of a cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is a cathedral city in the English county of Cambridgeshire; the surrounding fenland district takes its name. AISLE and ISLE are pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: The historic fenland area around the city was once raised ground surrounded by marsh, now a district of the county.

clue.text: Border height that's worn?

definitions.meaning: the stitched edge of a garment or piece of cloth
the level at which a skirt or dress ends, which rises and falls with fashion

explanation.definitionFit: It is both the edge of a skirt and the fashionable length at which skirts are worn.

clue.text: Champion setter perhaps

parts.note: a setter is a breed of gun dog, and a prize-winning one would literally be the best canine, the idiom for the person in charge

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names whoever is dominant or most successful, a winner among rivals.

clue.text: From a bulb this could be lit up

indicators.note: could be says these letters might be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A light bulb that might be switched on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges LIT UP. 'Bulb' suggests a lamp, but it is the flower bulb the plant grows from.
explanation.definitionFit: This spring flower grows each year from a planted bulb.

clue.text: Testy chap transferred money in the office

indicators.note: letters transferred are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: An irritable man moved some funds around at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transferred' rearranges the letters of TESTY CHAP; it also suggests money being moved, which fits the definition nicely.
explanation.definitionFit: A small float of cash kept in an office for minor expenses.

clue.text: Biased — could be wholly right

definitions.meaning: playfully, something entirely on the right, or the left, is all on a single flank

explanation.definitionFit: Unfair partiality favours one camp, and anything wholly to the right occupies only that half.

clue.text: Way to go round on leisurely walk

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
to roll is to turn over and over, going round

explanation.surface: Advice on how to take a relaxed amble, perhaps round a park.
explanation.definitionFit: An unhurried saunter is a relaxed walk.

clue.text: Obstinate train driver?

parts.note: an obstinate creature is a mule, and the person who drives a train of mules is not a locomotive engineer at all

explanation.definitionFit: A person who drives pack animals, the stubborn beasts famously hard to steer.

clue.text: Food Mario can prepare

indicators.note: to prepare is to make ready, here working the letters into a new shape

explanation.surface: An Italian man called Mario can cook something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepare' rearranges MARIO CAN; the Italian name suits the pasta answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This tube-shaped pasta is a food.

clue.text: Sophy, sickly child, consumed some medicine

indicators.note: these words say only part of the run is taken, a stretch inside the girl's name and the next word

explanation.surface: A poorly girl called Sophy took a dose of her medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumed some' points to letters spanning SoPHY SICkly. The answer is an old word for medicine, still found in 'physician'.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic term for a remedy or drug, especially a purgative.

clue.text: Before thought it had been planned in advance

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before
to have meditated is to have thought deeply

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a thing was deliberate all along.
explanation.definitionFit: A deliberate crime is one plotted beforehand rather than done on impulse.

clue.text: Meticulous without you and me in strict observance of etiquette

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letters for you and me are dropped

parts.note: punctilious means meticulous, fussily precise
you and me together are us

explanation.surface: Being careful without the two of us, you and me, in matters of strict social formality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes U and S, the last letters but one and last, from PUNCTILIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine point of correct behaviour, or scrupulous attention to such formality.

clue.text: Working like a horse?

parts.note: a working horse is strapped into its tack, and the idiom for being at work comes from that picture

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means at work, still employed, as a draught animal is when tacked up.

clue.text: We set about vegetable or flower

indicators.note: about can mean around, shaking the letters into another order

parts.note: a pea is a green vegetable

explanation.surface: We plant around a vegetable, or else a flower, in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges WE SET to make SWEET.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing plant grown for its fragrant blossom.

clue.text: It comes at the end of a four-week period

definitions.text: It comes at the end of a four-week period

parts.words: It comes at the end of a four-week period
parts.note: four weeks are twenty-eight days, so the day closing that span is the final ordinal of that count

explanation.definitionFit: Four times seven days ends on the day bearing that ordinal number.

clue.text: I name spot where it has been positioned

parts.note: a spot is a place

explanation.surface: I identify the location where something was put.
explanation.definitionFit: Something set or fixed in its proper position is where it belongs.

clue.text: Drive away Diane's gymnastic pupil

parts.note: Di is a short form of Diane, so Diane's is Di's
PE is physical education, the school gymnastic lesson
L is a learner, a pupil, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: Diane's athletic student chases something off.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a red L plate marks a learner driver, so L stands for any learner or pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispel fears or a crowd is to banish or scatter them.

clue.text: The man caught in charge rushed

parts.note: he refers to a man
caught gives CT

explanation.surface: A man has been arrested while in command of something in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: A frantic, frenzied pace feels hurried and busy.

clue.text: Lacey's partner in fighting crime losing point of being secretive

indicators.note: losing tells us a letter is taken away

parts.note: Cagney and Lacey were the two women detectives of the US police drama of that name
N, for north, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A TV cop reluctant to reveal her secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' drops N from CAGNEY; 'point' is a compass point, not a dot or an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Being wary and unwilling to give information is being guarded.

clue.text: Nora paid stranger having irrational fears

indicators.note: stranger means odder, so the letters are made odd by rearranging

explanation.surface: Nora paid a stranger because she was afraid of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stranger' looks like a noun for an unknown person, but it is the comparative adjective, signalling an anagram of NORA PAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Suffering unreasonable suspicion or anxiety, believing others mean harm.

clue.text: Relative coming from place in France, it is heard

indicators.note: it is heard means the word is spoken, a homophone

parts.note: Nice is a city on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: A family member arriving from somewhere in France, so we hear.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a family member.

clue.text: A game with us soldier having advance defence

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
GI is a US soldier
a is a dictionary abbreviation for advance, as in commerce

explanation.surface: A sporting match involving an American serviceman who is going forward to defend.
explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviation A for advance is in Chambers; it is not one solvers meet often.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal written justification of one's own beliefs or conduct is a defence of them.

clue.text: Grant immunity to former euro member before time

parts.note: ex- means former
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Excusing an ex-member of the European parliament from some duty just in time.
explanation.definitionFit: To free someone from an obligation or rule is to excuse them from it.

clue.text: A number in duplicate on shelter

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside another

parts.note: a duplicate is a copy

explanation.surface: Two of something kept on top of a covering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts A and N inside COPY after its C.
explanation.definitionFit: An overhead covering of cloth or branches gives cover from sun or rain.

clue.text: Wind, gusty, set in prematurely

indicators.note: in signals the shuffled letters go inside another word

parts.note: early means before the expected time, prematurely

indicators.note: gusty suggests letters blown about and scattered

explanation.surface: A gusty wind arrived ahead of schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' is the noun, not the verb. 'gusty' and 'in' read as weather words but are the anagram and container signals, giving STE from 'set'.
explanation.definitionFit: A breeze blowing from the east is named after that direction.
